rows.text: The snow child's cabin was filled with paintings of pure white. They had no names, so one could only point to them when speaking of them. Yet he never asked about color, for the "world" was but a flake of frost upon his lashes. Whether out of admiration or ill intent, people sent all manner of scenes to his little cabin, so that he might know the vibrant tapestry of the world beyond. He would run his fingers across those unfamiliar vistas, leaving trails of water on the canvas. Then, all that was pure white began to crumble... After what felt like an eternity, the snow child awoke. The mistake he had committed could never be undone, just as words carved into stone can only be struck through, never smoothed away. And so he returned to his cabin, shut the door, and buried every other color in the world beneath an endless, unrelenting snow.
